implementation_notes: std::iter::successors(Some(seed), step) is the standard library's unfold for linear structures: the closure receives &T and returns Option<T>, None ending the iteration, and the iterator is lazy so take/collect decide the extent. std::iter::from_fn covers steps whose next state is not the previous item (the closure owns mutable state), and Iterator::scan is the stateful middle ground. Tree-shaped unfolds are eager recursive builders over Box/Rc because ownership makes sharing awkward; an explicit Vec worklist keeps the stack bounded.
pitfalls: successors stores the produced item and calls the closure on &T, so the next state must be derivable from the previous item; when state and item differ, use from_fn or scan.
A recursive tree builder needs Box (or an arena) per node and still overflows the stack on deep structures: prefer an explicit Vec-based worklist.
Iterator adaptors capture the state by value, so cloning an unfold iterator clones the state and the two clones unfold independently from the same point.
